title: Induction Motor Parts
description: FanPedia's exploded view of an electric induction motor (p. 69) with ten numbered markers, leader lines and label strips above and below the drawing. Explore mode previews each part's name and description; quiz mode hides the labels and describes each part by its job, with two attempts, a hint after the first miss and mastery at 8 of 10 on the first attempt.

educational.audience: Adult professional development: new application engineers, sales staff, representatives and facilities staff
educational.topic: Parts of an electric induction motor
learningObjectives: The learner will identify the ten labeled parts of an electric induction motor on an exploded view, given each part's function.

accessibility.notes: The drawing is a labelled SVG group; every numbered marker is a focusable role=button and Tab walks them in number order; Enter or Space selects one; focus or hover previews its name and description. During the quiz the markers are named only 'Part n' until resolved, labels and leader lines are hidden, and hints never name the answer. Verdicts and prompts are announced through FP.announce (aria-live). ✓/✗ glyphs, solid/dashed borders and an 'Answer' badge pair with colour. Text is 12 px or larger; markers keep a constant pixel size; the label strips move below the drawing as a numbered list on narrow screens.

simulation.modelType: labeled diagram with locate quiz (FP.Overlay callout engine on FP.CalloutQuiz)
rules: Explore mode: hover or focus previews a part's name and description; click, Enter or Space opens it and counts it as visited; never scored.
Quiz mode: 10 prompts in a seeded shuffle (the same order for every learner; Start over reshuffles).
Two attempts per prompt; the first wrong answer shows a hint that does not name the answer; the second reveals the answer and counts as missed.
Selecting empty space uses no attempt.
Only first-attempt answers count toward mastery; mastery is 8 of 10.
assumptions: FanPedia p. 69 exploded view, with the printed labels removed and the manufacturer brand text on the nameplate painted over; marker positions are percentages of the image.
limitations: The drawing is FanPedia's typical TEFC induction motor, not a specific catalog motor; the lifting eye has no marker, and the 'Conduit wiring on motor with nameplate' inset photo of the original page is not shown.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Explore labelled markers on the real FanPedia drawing first, then retrieval practice: find each part from a description of its job, with a hint after the first miss and immediate correction.
keyQuestions: Which part tells you the motor's manufacturer, serial number and ratings?
Which parts turn, and which stay still?
On a TEFC motor, where does the cooling air enter and what does it blow over?
commonMisconceptions: The rotor is wired to the supply like the stator.
The external fan of a TEFC motor blows air over the windings.
The motor bearings sit in the frame rather than inside the endplates.
assessmentOpportunities: First-attempt score shown as 'First-attempt score: n of 10'; mastery is 8 of 10 on the first attempt.
